Exports OTLP **traces and logs** into documented BigQuery relational tables via
the [BigQuery Storage Write API](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/write-api).

The OpenTelemetry Collector has no BigQuery exporter. Getting traces and logs
into BigQuery for SQL analytics today means routing through Cloud Logging sinks,
standing up Pub/Sub plus Dataflow, or batch-loading files — an extra product
hop, an extra pipeline to operate, or manual work.

This component has exactly one job: **reliable transport with a stable,
documented schema.** It is not an analytics product. It does not aggregate,
sample, downsample, or interpret telemetry.

> **Status: pre-alpha.** The configuration surface, schema and factory wiring
> are real; the write path is not implemented yet and `pushTraceData` /
> `pushLogData` return an explicit error. See the milestones below.

## Design

Full design doc: **go/o11y-bq-exporter** (Google-internal). Section references
in the code and in this README point at it.

## Getting started

```yaml
exporters:
  bigquery:
    project: my-project
    dataset: otel
    spans_table: otel_spans
    logs_table: otel_logs

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [bigquery]
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [bigquery]
```

## Configuration

| Option                         | Default             | Description |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------- | ----------- |
| `project`                      | *required*          | Google Cloud project owning the destination dataset. |
| `dataset`                      | *required*          | Destination BigQuery dataset ID. |
| `spans_table`                  | `otel_spans`        | Destination table for OTLP spans. |
| `logs_table`                   | `otel_logs`         | Destination table for OTLP log records. |
| `auto_create.dataset`          | `false`             | Create the dataset if absent. Requires `auto_create.location`. |
| `auto_create.tables`           | `false`             | Create the destination tables if absent. |
| `auto_create.location`         | —                   | Dataset location used when creating a dataset. |
| `write.max_request_bytes`      | `9437184` (9 MiB)   | Our request-size headroom threshold, enforced after protobuf serialization and before `AppendRows`. Distinct from, and below, the API's own per-request limit. |
| `write.max_row_bytes`          | `1048576` (1 MiB)   | Rejects individual rows above this serialized size. |
| `write.max_inflight_requests`  | `1000`              | Bounds asynchronous in-flight appends. |
| `write.max_inflight_bytes`     | `104857600` (100 MiB) | Bounds memory held by in-flight appends. |
| `promote_attributes`           | `[]`                | Lifts named attributes into their own nullable top-level columns. |
| `sending_queue`                | collector defaults  | Standard `exporterhelper` queue, including the persistent queue. |
| `retry_on_failure`             | collector defaults  | Standard `exporterhelper` retry with backoff. |
| `timeout`                      | collector defaults  | Per-request timeout. |

`auto_create` is off by default deliberately: leaving it off keeps the exporter
on a write-only IAM path.

### Promoted attributes

Attributes live in a JSON bag by default. Promotion lifts a named attribute into
its own nullable column so it can be filtered and clustered on:

```yaml
exporters:
  bigquery:
    project: my-project
    dataset: otel
    promote_attributes:
      - attribute: gen_ai.system
        type: STRING
      - attribute: gen_ai.usage.input_tokens
        column: input_tokens
        type: INT64
```

Rules:

- Promoted columns are **nullable and additive**; adding one is a minor schema
  version bump.
- The attribute bag remains the source of truth. A promoted column is an index,
  not a replacement.
- Removing an entry from the config does **not** drop the column.
- Promoted columns are **excluded from the record fingerprint**, so a fleet
  running heterogeneous promotion configs still produces identical fingerprints
  for the same logical record.

## Delivery semantics

Delivery is **at-least-once**. The exporter writes on the Storage Write API
default stream, which is offset-free and requires no connection or stream-offset
bookkeeping. A retried append can therefore land the same logical record twice.

This is a deliberate choice, not a limitation we are working around. Measured
duplicate rates on the default stream are small, and read-time deduplication is
the proportionate answer for the overwhelming majority of consumers. Exactly-once
would mean committed-mode streams with per-stream offset management, lower
default quotas and materially more server-side orchestration.

Every row carries a deterministic identity so duplicates can be collapsed at
read time:

- **Spans**: `(trace_id, span_id)`.
- **Logs**: the typed tuple `(source_record_namespace, source_record_id)` when a
  producer supplies one, otherwise a content fingerprint.

The repo ships `otel_spans_dedup` and `otel_logs_dedup` **logical views** so the
default object an analyst touches is already deduplicated. See
[`internal/schema`](internal/schema/schema.go).

> **Known limit, stated rather than hidden:** for logs without a trusted
> `(source_record_namespace, source_record_id)` tuple, deduplication is
> content-equivalence rather than identity. Two genuinely distinct but
> byte-identical log records collapse into one. This is inherent to
> fingerprinting.

### Materializing the dedup view

If per-query scan cost matters, materialize it — but **not** as a
non-incremental materialized view. Background refresh and runtime merge read the
full baseline table, and only query jobs get partition and cluster pruning, so
at telemetry volume every refresh interval becomes a full-table scan.

Use a **scheduled `MERGE`** into a clean table instead, bounded to a recent
partition window. DML against rows written by the gRPC Storage Write API has no
streaming-buffer blackout, so a `MERGE` can run right up to the head of the
stream.

Keep the view regardless: duplicate classes outside the retry window (pipeline
fanout, multiple collectors exporting the same telemetry, upstream SDK retries)
are not bounded by the `MERGE` lookback. The view is the correctness backstop;
the `MERGE` is only ever the optimization.

## IAM

The least-privilege path for pre-created tables is a **write-only custom role**
centered on `bigquery.tables.updateData`, plus `bigquery.tables.get` for startup
validation. `roles/bigquery.dataEditor` is the convenient broader alternative,
not the least-privilege one. Create permissions are needed only when the
corresponding `auto_create` flag is on.

Startup permission preflight is **best-effort, not authoritative**: BigQuery
documents that `tables.testIamPermissions` is not intended for authorization
checking and may fail open, and `tables.get` proves metadata access rather than
write access. Preflight warns; it does not gate startup on its own verdict.

## What this deliberately does not do

- **Metrics.** The OTLP metrics signal needs its own relational design — five
  data-point types, delta versus cumulative temporality, exemplars, per-series
  identity. Getting that wrong freezes it into a versioned contract. It is an
  independent future proposal, not a missing feature.

  Note for agent telemetry: token counts and cost are typically emitted on
  *both* a metric and an event. Since this exporter ingests events, "no metrics
  support" does **not** mean "no token data".
- **Exactly-once.** See delivery semantics above.
- **Dead-letter queue.** Permanently invalid rows are counted and dropped, not
  quarantined. There is no payload to replay and no second retention, IAM or
  security surface.
- **Aggregation, sampling or rollups.** Use the Collector's processors.

| --------- | -------- |
| **M1** | Write path on the Storage Write API default stream; schema v1 for traces and logs; request sizing and the error matrix; throughput target validated. |
